reason: The text (Job 1 in Hebrew) presents Job as a model of personal righteousness (tam v'yashar—blameless and upright) characterized primarily by his fear of God and spiritual piety. While the passage mentions his large household of servants as part of his wealth, it does not describe or emphasize care for their welfare as a defining leadership principle. The narrative focuses on Job's individual moral character, his material prosperity, and his pious response to trials, not on his relationship to or care for the common people under his authority. The servants appear only as possessions that are destroyed in the calamities, without any indication of how he treated them or that such treatment was part of his exemplary model.
